For The General Humanities paper, this paper will consist of general essay questions on History, Philosophy, Geography, Economics, Politics and Current Affairs. Candidates will be asked to choose two essays from any section. These questions can be on the same topic, or spread across different areas. Evidence of wider and engaged reading, general historical and political knowledge and the ability to employ a high standard of written English will ensure a candidate is well prepared.

*Example (1): If a candidate wishes to study Economics at A Level (or History, Philosophy, Geography, Politics and Current Affairs) they should sit the General Humanities paper. This paper will consist of general essay questions on History, Philosophy, Geography, Economics, Politics and Current Affairs. Candidates will be asked to choose two essays from any section; in this candidate’s case, one of the essays would be Economics.

*Example (2): If a student’s AS subject choices are Eng Lit, Politics, History, BS/Econ, as well as EAL and English Literature papers, for the General Humanities paper, the student should write three essays (instead of the two); History, Economics and Politics & Current Affairs.

If an applicant wishes to study a humanities subject at A Level they must sit the General Humanities Paper as one of their two optional papers

For The General Humanities paper, this paper will consist of general essay questions on History, Philosophy, Geography, Economics and Politics. Candidates will be asked to answer two essays from one section. Evidence of wider and engaged reading, general historical and political knowledge and the ability to employ a high standard of written English will ensure a candidate is well prepared.

*Example (1): If a candidate wishes to study Economics at A Level (or History, Philosophy, Geography and Politics) they should sit the General Humanities paper. Candidates will be asked to answer two essays from one section; in this candidate’s case, the essays would be Economics.

*Example (2): If a student’s AS subject choices are Eng Lit, Politics, History, BS/Econ, as well as EAL and English Literature papers, for the General Humanities paper, the student should write three essays (instead of the two); History, Economics and Politics.

aaremarks:
The test is taken in 2 parts – each strictly 10 minutes long

•	First of all ask the candidate to enter their details on the Answer Sheet (name etc)
•	Ask them to turn their answer sheet over and to find the column showing examples
•	Ask them to open their booklet to Page 1 – Part 1 Examples
•	Ask the candidate to read the instructions and to fill in the gaps and answer the remaining questions in the example column
•	Give them time to complete these.  When completed, read out the answers to them as follows:
•	“Correct answers to the examples you’ve been doing are as follows: 5, 4, 64, 4, 25, 5).”
•	Then ask them to turn to Page 3 and ask them to work through the questions in Section One in order, using the columns on the answer sheet for their answers.
•	Allow 10 minutes only for this section.

Then follow the same procedure with examples for Section 2.
•	When they have filled in the gaps in the example column, read out as follows:
•	“Correct answers to the examples you have been doing are 2,3,3,2,1”.
•	Then ask them to turn to Page 9 and begin Section Two, answering the questions in order, using the columns on the answer sheet.
•	Allow 10 minutes only for this section.

aaremarks:
The test is taken in 2 parts – each strictly 10 minutes long

•	First of all ask the candidate to enter their details on the Answer Sheet (name etc)
•	Ask them to turn their answer sheet over and to find the column showing examples
•	Ask them to open their booklet to Page 1 – Part 1 Examples
•	Ask the candidate to read the instructions and to fill in the gaps and answer the remaining questions in the example column
•	Give them time to complete these.  When completed, read out the answers to them as follows:
•	“Correct answers to the examples you’ve been doing are as follows: 5, 4, 64, 4, 25, 5).”
•	Then ask them to turn to Page 3 and ask them to work through the questions in Section One in order, using the columns on the answer sheet for their answers.
•	Allow 10 minutes only for this section.

Then follow the same procedure with examples for Section 2.
•	When they have filled in the gaps in the example column, read out as follows:
•	“Correct answers to the examples you have been doing are 2,3,3,2,1”.
•	Then ask them to turn to Page 9 and begin Section Two, answering the questions in order, using the columns on the answer sheet.
•	Allow 10 minutes only for this section.

examformat: Part 1 and part 2- Time Limit for each part is 10 minutes exclusive of the preliminary examples. With answer sheet
aaremarks:
The test is taken in 2 parts – each strictly 10 minutes long

•	First of all ask the candidate to enter their details on the Answer Sheet (name etc)
•	Ask them to turn their answer sheet over and to find the column showing examples
•	Ask them to open their booklet to Page 1 – Part 1 Examples
•	Ask the candidate to read the instructions and to fill in the gaps and answer the remaining questions in the example column
•	Give them time to complete these.  When completed, read out the answers to them as follows:
•	“Correct answers to the examples you’ve been doing are as follows: 5, 4, 64, 4, 25, 5).”
•	Then ask them to turn to Page 3 and ask them to work through the questions in Section One in order, using the columns on the answer sheet for their answers.
•	Allow 10 minutes only for this section.

Then follow the same procedure with examples for Section 2.
•	When they have filled in the gaps in the example column, read out as follows:
•	“Correct answers to the examples you have been doing are 2,3,3,2,1”.
•	Then ask them to turn to Page 9 and begin Section Two, answering the questions in order, using the columns on the answer sheet.
•	Allow 10 minutes only for this section.

aaremarks:
For TS group exam

From Boarding Admissions :
- expect all students to have achieved at least a 6/B grade in GCSE 3D or DT
- all students will be required to send through an electronic portfolio of their work to the above e-mail address including evidence of all or some of the following :- 

1. 3D drawing skills - demonstrating the ability to produce good quality oblique, isometric or perspective drawings. 
2. Clear presentation sheets of design ideas including rendering of design drawings and annotation. 
3. Ability to produce models in a variety of media - e.g. modelling clay, card, paper, foam board, CAD etc. 
4. Analysis of the work of other designers, both contemporary and historic. 
5. Evidence of CAD/CAM would be useful, however depending on the quality of the rest of their portfolio this is not necessarily essential. 
6. 3D Design work produced in a variety of materials showing evidence of a range of practical techniques. 
7. Work demonstrating an understanding of various methods of manufacture using wood, metal and plastic. 

Photographs of selected work (drawings, paintings, sculpture, photography, textiles, printmaking etc.).  The student is not expected to have examples of work from each of these areas.  Please upload at least 10 photographs showing the student’s best work.  Please ensure everything is clearly labelled.

- Pupils respond to a series of statements about school and learning. - PASS takes just 20 minutes to complete so it can be easily administered during a form period. It can be taken on any device and is available in 26 languages.
